brief.greeting: Good morning. Your night just got a firmware upgrade and a 145‑billion‑parameter model to stare at.

stories.headline: Edge0 drops a 145B text generator
stories.body: **Massive but manageable:** Edge0/Edge0-145B-NVFP4 hit Hugging Face with 145 billion parameters and 33,819 downloads, showing huge models can still attract interest. It runs on NVFP4 precision, trading a bit of quality for speed.
stories.why: If you tinker with inference, it proves scale isn’t limited to data‑center GPUs.

stories.headline: DIVINER adds occult synth to Cardputer
stories.body: **Synthesizer meets pocket PC:** The DIVINER firmware plugs occult‑synth capabilities into the M5 Cardputer, turning the handheld into a mini‑modular synth without extra hardware.
stories.why: Engineers can experiment with audio DSP on a familiar dev board.

stories.headline: LibreTranslate offers offline translation API
stories.body: **Self‑hosted language bridge:** LibreTranslate provides a free, open‑source translation service you can run locally, eliminating cloud latency and data‑privacy concerns.
stories.why: Useful for edge devices that need on‑device multilingual support.

quick_hits.text: **Terminal AI:** Qwen‑code runs code generation directly in your shell.
**Hydroponics monitor:** Joziti’s cloud‑based system tracks pH, temperature, and conductivity at home.
**PostScript interpreter:** New tutorial walks you through building an RPN‑based interpreter.
**Remote control:** IRis learning remote stores infrared codes for thousands of devices with five buttons.
**CPU inference library:** ggml offers a C++ tensor engine optimized for running models on CPUs.

highlights.title: DIVINER: Occult Synth Firmware for the Cardputer
highlights.summary: DIVINER is custom firmware that adds occult‑synth functionality to the M5 Cardputer handheld device.
highlights.detail: The firmware repurposes the Cardputer's hardware for experimental audio synthesis, demonstrating the flexibility of the platform for hobbyist firmware projects.

highlights.title: LibreTranslate/LibreTranslate
highlights.summary: LibreTranslate provides a free, open‑source machine‑translation API that can be self‑hosted and run offline.
highlights.detail: The service supports multiple language pairs and can be deployed on modest hardware, offering an alternative to cloud‑based translators for privacy‑focused applications.

highlights.title: Tencent/LoopForge
highlights.summary: LoopForge is a self‑hosted platform that orchestrates coding agents like CodeBuddy, Codex, and Claude with scriptable workflows and approval gates.
highlights.detail: It lets teams define local pipelines for AI‑assisted code generation, insert human review steps, and integrate multiple models, facilitating secure and customizable development automation.

highlights.title: ggml-org/ggml
highlights.summary: ggml is a C++ tensor library optimized for machine‑learning inference on CPUs.
highlights.detail: The library focuses on minimal dependencies and high performance for transformer models, enabling developers to run large language models locally without GPU acceleration.

highlights.title: FujiwaraChoki/supoclip
highlights.summary: Supoclip is an open-source Python implementation that serves as an alternative to OpusClip.
highlights.detail: The project is listed on GitHub trending and aims to replicate OpusClip's video‑clip generation capabilities while remaining fully open source, making it easy to integrate into custom pipelines.

items.title: Model: Edge0/Edge0-145B-NVFP4
items.summary: Edge0/Edge0-145B-NVFP4 is a 145‑billion‑parameter text‑generation model on Hugging Face with 33,819 downloads.
items.detail: The model targets large‑scale language tasks and is part of the Edge0 series optimized for NVIDIA FP4 precision. It has attracted moderate community interest, reflected in its like count.

items.title: Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
items.detail: The model supports converting visual inputs into textual descriptions and has become one of the most downloaded multimodal models on the platform, indicating strong demand for such capabilities.

items.title: Model: higurashi-ai/Haru-4B
items.summary: higurashi-ai/Haru-4B is a 4‑billion‑parameter audio‑to‑audio model on Hugging Face with 1,262 downloads.
items.detail: Haru‑4B focuses on tasks like voice conversion and audio style transfer, offering a compact alternative to larger audio models while gathering a niche user base.

items.title: DIVINER: Occult Synth Firmware for the Cardputer
items.summary: DIVINER is custom firmware that adds occult‑synth functionality to the M5 Cardputer handheld device.
items.detail: The firmware repurposes the Cardputer's hardware for experimental audio synthesis, demonstrating the flexibility of the platform for hobbyist firmware projects.

items.title: A Hazeltine 1420 Lives Again
items.summary: A recreated Hazeltine 1420 terminal has been brought back to life using modern components.
items.detail: The project rebuilds the classic terminal's display and keyboard interfaces, allowing vintage software to run on contemporary hardware while preserving historical computing experiences.

items.title: Bringing a Cloud Based Monitor Home
items.summary: Joziti built a cloud‑based monitor for home hydroponics, tracking temperature, pH, and conductivity.
items.detail: The system streams sensor data to a remote dashboard, enabling real‑time adjustments and data logging for hobby growers seeking tighter environmental control.

items.title: IRis Learning Remote Has Five Buttons, Supports Thousands of Devices
items.summary: The IRis learning remote features five buttons and can store infrared codes for thousands of devices.
items.detail: It revives the once‑popular universal IR remote concept while keeping the hardware simple. The device learns codes from existing remotes, making it useful for DIY home‑automation projects without needing complex setups.

items.title: RPN Loved Honk If (or, Write Your Own PostScript Interpreter)
items.summary: A tutorial walks readers through building a PostScript‑style interpreter using reverse Polish notation concepts.
items.detail: The guide ties together ideas from HP calculators, Forth, and classic laser‑printer languages, offering code snippets and explanations for each interpreter component. It targets hobbyists who enjoy low‑level language design.

items.title: Reverse Engineer that USB Device in Style
items.summary: The article shows how to capture and decode USB traffic with open‑source tools to reverse‑engineer proprietary devices.
items.detail: It recommends using packet sniffers and USB protocol analyzers, then demonstrates extracting command sequences for custom driver development. The approach helps developers avoid closed‑source driver lock‑in.

items.title: Helldez/BigMoeOnEdge
items.summary: BigMoeOnEdge is a C++ tool that enables running frontier‑size mixture‑of‑experts models larger than device RAM on phones, laptops and other edge hardware via adaptive streaming on top of llama.cpp.
items.detail: It provides lossless execution on stock llama.cpp, supports any hardware, OS, model and quantization, and exposes a local OpenAI‑compatible server, allowing developers to serve huge MoE models without cloud resources.

items.title: QwenLM/qwen-code
items.summary: Qwen‑code is an open-source AI coding agent that runs directly in the terminal, allowing code generation and assistance from the command line.
items.detail: Hosted on GitHub, the agent integrates with shell workflows, enabling developers to invoke AI‑powered coding help without leaving their console environment.
